Andreessen Horowitz is launching an ‘academy’ with no homework and partnerships with Palantir, Google, and Meta

Venture‑capital firm Andreessen Horowitz announced the launch of the Horowitz Andreessen Academy, a new program aimed at creating a pipeline for young talent to build or join Silicon Valley startups. The academy will operate without traditional homework assignments, positioning itself as a hands‑on experience for participants. Ten industry partners have been confirmed: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit and Stripe. Funding for the initiative totals $42 million, led by Andreessen Horowitz itself. According to the firm, the academy will connect learners directly with the partner companies, offering mentorship, project work and potential pathways into full‑time roles. The model reflects a growing trend among venture firms to cultivate talent internally rather than relying solely on external hiring. Observers note that the involvement of major tech players such as Google, Meta and OpenAI could give the program significant reach and credibility. The academy is slated to begin operations later this year, with enrollment details to be released shortly. What to watch: Enrollment numbers and the first cohort’s outcomes as the academy begins.

How to add extra Ethernet ports if your router doesn't have enough

In many home and office environments, the number of wired devices can quickly outpace the physical connectivity options provided by standard networking hardware. Ethernet ports are often in short supply on routers, leaving users to choose which devices get a stable wired connection and which must rely on wireless signals.

For those who run low on available ports, there is a practical solution that does not involve replacing the primary router. A cheap device is available that allows users to add more Ethernet ports to their existing setup without any significant fuss. This hardware expansion is designed to be a straightforward solution, requiring minimal technical knowledge to implement effectively.

The addition of extra ports ensures that various devices can maintain a consistent connection. By using an affordable expansion device, users can bypass the limitations of their router’s original design. This method provides a reliable way to scale a local network as more wired equipment is acquired.

The simplicity of this solution makes it an attractive option for users who want to avoid the complexities of network management. It offers a direct way to increase capacity while keeping the existing router as the central hub of the network.

What to watch: Whether router manufacturers begin to include more integrated ports in future models to keep up with the increasing density of wired devices.

Microsoft has announced a significant restructuring of its Xbox division, marking a major shift in how its game franchises are managed. This consolidation represents a strategic pivot for the company, centralizing the management of its most iconic titles under the Activision banner. By integrating these franchises, Microsoft aims to streamline development pipelines and enhance operational efficiency across its portfolio.

The restructuring reflects a continued effort to optimize the Xbox brand following recent financial pressures and market adjustments. While specific details on the operational changes remain limited, the transfer of these flagship titles signals a new chapter for their respective development teams.
